sentences.text: The petitioner is the 4th accused in Crime No.793 of 2022 registered by the Guruvayoor Police Station, Thrissur, alleging that the accused persons in the above crime have committed the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. The petitioner has filed this Criminal Miscellaneous Case to quash Annexure A1 FIR and all further proceedings in the above crime on the assertion that, even if the allegations in the FIR are taken on their face value, the same would not attract the offences alleged against the petitioner.
In fact, the petitioner is only an I.T. professional, who has been rendering services to the accused in the crime.
Therefore, the petitioner can no way be said to have any culpability in the crime.
Hence, the proceedings may be quashed.

The essence of the prosecution case is that, 05.09.2021, the 1st accused, the Global Director of the company named 'My Club Traders', along with the other accused persons, including the petitioner,
in furtherance of their common intention, went to the house of the defacto complainant and collected Rs.1,50,000/- from him on the assurance of doubling the investment in one year.
Subsequently, they also received another Rs.2,00,000/- on the same false promise.
However, the accused failed to pay any profit and refused to return the capital.

sentences.text: The Investigating Officer has filed a statement, inter alia, stating that the petitioner is a history sheeter.

He is involved in 10 other crimes of a similar nature registered by various police stations in Thrissur District, for allegedly committing the same offences and also the offences under Sections 3 and 21 of t he Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act.

sentences.text: The petitioner is absconding.
There are 2026:KER:19790 CRL.MC NO. 11511 OF 2025 specific overt acts alleged against the petitioner.

5 I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.

6. The learned counsel for the petitioner reiterates the contentions in the Crl.M.C.
7.
The learned Public Prosecutor seriously opposes the Crl.M.C.
She submits that in addition to the petitioner being a history sheeter, he has not got himself enlarged on bail in the above crime.
There are specific overt acts attributed against the petitioner.
Hence, the Crl.M.C. may be dismissed.

8. On going through Annexure A1 FIR, I find that there are specific overt acts alleged against the petitioner, that he along with other accused had induced the defacto complainant to invest money in the company named My Club Traders on the assurance of doubling the investment in one year.

Furthermore, in the statement filed by the 2026:KER:19790 CRL.MC NO. 11511 OF 2025 Investigating Officer it is seen that the petitioner is an accused in 10 other crimes of a similar nature by the various police stations in Thrissur District.
Moreover, it is reported that the petitioner has not got himself enlarged on bail till date in a crime, which is registered in the year 2022.

9. In Balmukund Singh Gautam v. State of Madhya Pradesh [2026 KHC 6125], the Hon'ble Supreme Court has categorically held that this Court may not exercise the inherent powers under Section 528 of the BNSS unless the accused persons subject themselves to the jurisdiction of the concerned court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
10. In the celebrated decision in State of Haryana and others v. Bhajan Lal and others [1992 Supp (1)
SCC 335], the Hon'ble Supreme Court has laid down exhaustive principles to quash a criminal proceeding.

SCC 335]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The salient principle is that, if the allegations in the complaint are 2026:KER:19790 CRL.MC NO. 11511 OF 2025 taken at their face value, they do not attract the offence; the inherent powers of this Court can be exercised.

On a careful analysis of the allegations in the FIR and on prima facie finding that, if the allegations are taken on their face value, the same would attract the offences alleged against the petitioner and further that the petitioner is a history sheeter, who has not got himself enlarged on bail, even after lapse of more than four years, I am satisfied that this is not a fit case to exercise the inherent powers of this Court under Section 528 of the BNSS.
The Crl.M.C. is devoid of any merits and is consequently dismissed.
